# A secret-scan-ok marker in a closed comment passes without a reason

## Context

Successor of #18832, which PR #18906 resolved. @neo-opus-grace found this in her review of #18906 (review 5249734191). Measured at `dev@3bd9c46e8f`.

## The Problem

`check-secrets` lets a line keep a credential-shaped literal if the line carries `secret-scan-ok: <reason>`. A marker without a reason is reported as `allow-marker-without-reason` (#18832, AC-5). The guard takes everything after the marker, up to the end of the line, as the reason. So a comment's own closing token counts as one.

`findSecrets` on a synthetic key-shaped line:

| Marker on the key's line | Result |
|---|---|
| `// secret-scan-ok:` | `allow-marker-without-reason` |
| `<!-- secret-scan-ok: -->` | nothing: the key is excused |
| `/* secret-scan-ok: */` | nothing |
| `{/* secret-scan-ok: */}` | nothing |
| `<!-- secret-scan-ok: a revoked sample -->` | nothing (correct) |

The incident behind #18832 was in a Markdown file. There, an HTML comment is exactly the form a marker takes.

## The Architectural Reality

- `buildScripts/util/check-secrets.mjs`: `allowRE = /secret-scan-ok:\s*(\S.*)?$/`. `findSecrets` accepts any captured text as a reason.
- The marker is read on every line, before the patterns and independently of them. The guard's own `export const ALLOW_MARKER = 'secret-scan-ok:';` line carries it, followed by `';`. A rule that only demands a letter would therefore report that line (Grace's second point).
- No other tracked file uses the marker (`git grep`, outside the guard and its spec).

## The Fix

- A reason is text with at least one letter or digit. Closers and punctuation (`-->`, `*/`, `*/}`, `';`) are not a reason.
- Read the marker only on a line that carries a credential-shaped match. There, a marker with a reason excuses the line, and one without a reason is `allow-marker-without-reason`. On any other line a marker excuses nothing, so there is nothing to report. That also leaves the definition line alone.
- Spec additions:
  - one row per closer: a finding;
  - a closed comment with a reason: excused;
  - a reasonless marker on a credential-free line: no finding.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `<!-- secret-scan-ok: -->`, `/* secret-scan-ok: */` and `{/* secret-scan-ok: */}` on a key's line each report `allow-marker-without-reason`. Each arm is red on `dev`.
- [ ] AC-2: a closed comment with a reason still excuses its line, and `// secret-scan-ok:` still reports.
- [ ] AC-3: `--all` over the tracked tree stays clean, the guard's own source included.

## Out of Scope

- **A guard run through a symlinked path exits 0.** `node <symlinked checkout>/buildScripts/util/check-secrets.mjs <file with a key>` exits 0 silently, while the same file through the real path exits 1 (measured). The CLI block compares `process.argv[1]` with `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` without resolving symlinks, and sibling guards use equivalent comparisons. `lint-staged` and CI invoke the guard by a relative path. This is captured as a defect-note, and gets its own ticket if promoted.
- Whether a one-word reason is an honest one. A reviewer reads the reason in the diff, as #18832 designed.
